title: Service account lifecycle, ownership, and provisioning flows for RBAC v2
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: Our current service account story is fragmented: creation via API/Console has divergent defaults, ownership is optional leading to orphans, and least-privilege templates exist but are not enforced at lifecycle events. With RBAC v2 and stricter audit requirements for Private deployments, we need a single, auditable provisioning and ownership model that integrates with SSO/SAML, supports templated least-privilege roles, enforces rotation/expiry, and surfaces ownership in the Console and audit logs.

Scope: Define and implement the service account lifecycle (create, claim/assign owner, rotate credentials, expire/revoke, decommission), Console UX for admin/service owner workflows, enforcement hooks for least-privilege templates at creation and role-change time, API endpoints for automated provisioning, and audit-log entries that capture owner, template used, and reason. Ensure compatibility with RBAC v2 role bindings and SSO identity mapping.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement secret storage backends (KMS/HSM integrations are separate), nor the cross-account federation flows for multi-tenant SaaS customers (handled in a follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Console: Admins can create service accounts and must choose an ownership model (individual, team, or system) during provisioning.
Ownership: Every service account has an owner field populated; orphaned accounts automatically enter an 'unclaimed' state and are surfaced in the Admin Dashboard.
Templates: Creation API / Console enforces a selected least-privilege template; if no template is selected, creation is blocked for production tier accounts.
RBAC v2 mapping: Service account role assignments are expressed as RBAC v2 bindings and visible in the role-trace UI.
Audit logging: Each lifecycle event (create, update, claim, rotate, revoke, expire) emits an audit log record with actor, owner, template_id, and justification fields.
SSO tie-in: When a user creates/claims a service account via SSO/SAML session, the audit record includes the SAML assertion id and mapped external_id.
Rotation/expiry: Service accounts support optional credential expiry; rotation endpoint exists in the API and is covered by integration tests.
Automation: Provisioning API supports idempotent create with template override and returns a traceable request_id for correlation in logs.
design_decisions: Model: Represent service accounts as first-class RBAC v2 principals with a required 'owner' attribute (user or team).
Templates: Keep least-privilege templates centrally versioned; template application occurs at creation and on explicit role-change events (not implicitly on every policy change).
Claims: Require an explicit claim flow in Console for manual assignment; provide a 'claim by owner email' API that sends ownership claim emails for verification to reduce orphan rate.
Audit: Use structured audit events (JSON) with fixed schema (event_type, actor_id, owner_id, template_id, justification, saml_assertion_id, request_id) to make downstream analysis and alerts easier.
SSO Mapping: Map SAML attributes to Redwood user id at authentication time and include external_id in audit events for customer compliance.
Security posture: Default to deny-for-production — blocking service account creation without a template for production-labeled orgs until an approved template is selected.
tradeoffs: Usability vs Safety: Requiring template selection increases friction for self-serve but prevents privilege creep; mitigate with curated 'basic' templates and one-click approvals for small teams.

Automation complexity: Sending verification emails for claims adds latency to programmatic provisioning; we provide a service-to-service 'pre-approved' flag for infra automation that requires an org admin bootstrap step.
Audit verbosity: Structured logs increase storage/costs; we retain high-fidelity events for 90 days by default and allow enterprise customers to opt into longer retention as an add-on.
tasks: API: POST /service-accounts create with template_id, owner_hint, expiration_seconds, justification -> returns request_id
API: PATCH /service-accounts/:id/claim owner_id -> verification email flow + audit event
Console: New 'Service accounts' admin page with filters for orphaned/unclaimed and owner contact info
Backend: Enforce template validation logic and RBAC v2 binding generation codepath
Audit: Implement structured audit event writer and ensure events are emitted for all lifecycle changes
SSO: Include saml_assertion_id and external_id in auth context available to provisioning endpoints
Tests: Integration tests for create/claim/rotate/revoke paths and audit event assertions
Migration: Backfill owner for existing service accounts marked 'created_by' where possible; orphan others into 'unclaimed' and send owner-review notifications
